_comment: Per-user settings. FIRST RUN: fill in jira.site_url, your boards, and slack.channel_id (or just tell Claude your channel name and it will resolve and save it). Claude reads this at Step 0 of every run. Values left null are resolved at runtime and written back here.

boards._comment: Your boards in priority order. rank 0 = highest. usesSprints false for Kanban/backlog boards so the sprint filter is skipped instead of silently returning nothing.

EXAMPLE.name: Replace with your project key and name

ranking._comment: Single source of truth for ranking weights — render_canvas.py, render_dashboard.py, and shortlist.py all read this via --weights instead of hardcoding their own copies. Editing here is enough; no script needs a code change. Sort order is: board rank, then Bug-type first, then this weighted score.

slack._comment: channel_id null = Claude asks once, resolves it, and writes it back. canvas_id null = a new canvas is created on first run and its id saved here. NEVER ship someone else's channel_id or canvas_id — they are per-workspace and per-user, and another person's ids will fail with a permissions error.

salesforce._comment: How to reach org metadata, in preference order. All read-only.

deployment._comment: Hard guardrail. never_autonomous means no write or deploy EVER happens without the user explicitly approving that specific change in that turn. Scheduled and unattended runs are always read-only regardless of this setting.
